# Reading the opened lockbox

*Sections S1–S3 of the test plan's scorecard layout (docs/test-plan.md §0.16), written on 2026-11-09 from the recorded result. `docs/scorecard.md` is regenerated by `uv run blackout evaluate`; this page is the fixed reading of the one opening. The commits it names are in the private development archive, not in the public repository (README, project notes).*

## S1. Verdict (A): the pre-registered curve on the locked storms, scored once

Every number here is read from `data/processed/lockbox_result.json`, written by one run of `blackout lockbox` at 2026-11-08 23:55:07 PST (code `7fd2732`, committed as `50d572e`). The bar (`2f534f9`, 2026-11-08 21:21) says a storm passes at ±60 when (1) the curve's county error is below the wind-only guess's on the same rows, (2) the pooled Spearman of night-to-night changes is at least 0.3, and (3) the median restore-day error over hit counties is at most 2.0 days. ±30 and ±90 are reported beside ±60 and do not enter the verdict. Error is mean |estimate − official| in percentage points over scored county-nights (hit counties, event nights, status `ok`, covered, usable official count).

**Verdict: FAIL.** Neither storm passes at ±60: both beat wind-only and both fail the agreement and restore-day conditions, at every window. Under the committed rule (pass if both pass, partial if one does, fail otherwise) the per-storm results recomputed here give "fail", which is the recorded string. Drop rule: neither storm was dropped (`table.drop_check`: Helene 265 of 277 hit counties had an `ok` night within 7 days of landfall, share 0.957; Milton 73 of 74, share 0.986), so the verdict covers both storms.

## S2. The shipped model: the registered satellite test (B) and the hybrid for information

**(B) Does the satellite add to wind + timing? Verdict: YES.** Registered in `2187e37` with edge rules in `7fd2732`, both before the opening. Per locked storm, on the pass bar's scored rows, the hybrid must (1) have lower error than `wind_timing` on county-nights officially at least 10% out, and (2) higher AUC for county-nights at least half out. A storm is evaluable with at least 10 rows at least 10% out; the AUC condition counts only with at least 10 rows at least half out, otherwise the storm rests on the error condition. Recomputed here from the recorded `satellite_increment` rows, the flags and the verdict match the record.

| Storm | Rows ≥ 10% out | Evaluable | Error ≥ 10%: hybrid vs wind + timing (pp) | Difference | (1) lower | Rows ≥ 50% out | AUC condition evaluable | AUC ≥ 50%: hybrid vs wind + timing | Difference | (2) higher | Passes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| helene2024 | 566 | yes | 33.0 vs 35.1 | −2.1 | yes | 175 | yes | 0.784 vs 0.784 | +0.0006 | yes | **yes** |
| milton2024 | 41 | yes | 12.9 vs 15.0 | −2.0 | yes | 4 | no (fewer than 10 rows) | 0.959 vs 0.956 | +0.003 (not counted) | rests on error | **yes** |
| both pooled | 607 | | 31.6 vs 33.7 | −2.1 | | 179 | | 0.793 vs 0.783 | +0.010 | | |

How to read it: the differences are the evidence and the label is a sign test on two storms. The error gain is about 2 points on both storms; the AUC gain on Helene is 0.0006, level to three decimals. Under leave-one-storm-out on the main storms (design loop) the same increment was −1.6 pp pooled and favourable on 5 of 8 storms; under forward chaining −0.6 pp.

The hybrid's restore counties (129 on Helene) are fewer than the curve's (252) because the bar's rule needs the next clear night to confirm a drop and the hybrid's estimates bounce: of 269 hit covered counties, 118 drop to 10% or below but are never confirmed, 12 never drop after their maximum and 10 have fewer than two clear nights (D-3). Trigger view, recorded run (truth read as the first raw official value after 72 hours, D-6): on Helene the hybrid paid 17 counties, 5 of them correctly, and missed 47 of 52; the curve paid none. Under D-6's truth (EAGLE-I's readings either side of the 72-hour mark, after the over-count rule) and against a band-64 wind trigger (both defined after the opening) the hybrid misses 44 of the 48 half-out counties it could judge (10 unknown) and the wind trigger 46 of 50, with 13 and 19 wrong payments.

## S3. The reading

Per the acceptance definition of `docs/test-plan.md` §0.14 (written after the opening, before the result was read; logged as D-2): (A) = **fail**, (B) = **yes**.

**Reading: NOT WORKING as pre-registered.** The pre-registered night-light curve did not pass the committed bar on Helene or Milton. The secondary, post hoc model's satellite increment held up on the locked storms: the hybrid beat its no-satellite twin on error where at least 10% out by about 2 points on both storms, with AUC level on Helene and not evaluable on Milton. That is evidence that the night-light reading carries some information about outages once wind band and timing are known; it is not evidence that the shipped model is good enough for the portfolio example's questions.

Conditions behind the reading:
- **Integrity (§0.3), what has been checked in this step:** the recorded code hashes match `model.py`, `hybrid.py`, `ranges.py`, `evaluate.py` and `final.py` at `7fd2732`; `run_at_utc` (07:55:07Z) lies between the commit times of `7fd2732` (07:54:45Z) and `50d572e` (07:57:13Z); `training_tables` lists the eight main storms with Beryl as `county_nights_beryl2024.parquet` (VJ146A2); the verdict string follows the committed rule given the per-storm passes; the satellite test's flags recompute from the recorded increment rows; neither locked storm meets the drop rule; the locked tables' customers match `counties.load_counties` (LB-43, checked 2026-11-09 00:05). **Open until D-20 and S1a:** the recorded provenance says `working_tree_dirty: true` and does not say what was dirty; the run had no opening marker and no guard against a rerun, so the single-run statement rests on the person who ran it and on the prediction files' timestamps (all written at 23:55); the reproduction at the recorded commit (LB-42) has not run. The reading stands if those checks pass or their findings are disclosed beside the recorded numbers; nothing here changes the recorded numbers.
- **Wording rules.** LOSO numbers for the hybrid and `wind_timing` are "design loop". Any number from code written after `50d572e` is "defined after the opening" (the D-6 trigger truth, the D-3 restore split, the D-11 ranges, S14's pre-Milton Helene). Slices are "exploratory". Ian's row is "LOSO".
- **Descriptive numbers that qualify the wording, from the recorded run and the design loop:** the hybrid fails pass-bar condition 1 on both locked storms (7.16 vs 7.00 pp; 2.20 vs 1.75); its night-to-night agreement is 0.18–0.19, under the bar's 0.3; its restore-day error is 5 days; under LOSO its county error (2.95 pp) is worse than "nothing" (2.17); forward chaining raises its error on rows at least 10% out from 24.1 to 28.7 pp. "Nothing" meets condition 3 on 4 of 8 main storms under LOSO and the hybrid on 3 of 8, so condition 3 is a weak test (S8, D-3). The bar's condition 1 comparator is diluted by baseline nights (D-13), so beating it on both storms is the least informative part of the record.
- **What a reader may claim.** The pre-registered method is not working. The satellite's increment over wind and timing is positive on two held-out storms and small. The app shows the hybrid's estimates and ranges labelled as a storm-context model; those estimates were not held out on the main storms and carry the "recorded run" label on Helene and Milton. The next clean test is a storm not yet built, held out before any fit.
